questions.question_text: Is the curve $f(x) = x^{3} + 4x^{2} - 5x + 7$ concave up or concave down at $x = -2$?

options.why: Substituted $x = 2$ rather than $x = -2$ into $f''(x) = 6x + 8$.

options.text: Neither, because the curve is decreasing at $x = -2$
options.why: Used the sign of $f'(-2) = -9$, which gives decreasing, and treated that as the concavity.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly explains why $y = 4x^{2} - 9x + 2$ is concave up for every value of $x$?

options.why: Tested the first derivative instead of the second, and $8x - 9$ is not positive for all $x$ in any case.
Differentiated only once and labelled the result $y''$.

options.text: The coefficient of $x$ is negative, so the parabola opens upwards.
options.why: Read the coefficient $b = -9$; it is the sign of $a$, not $b$, that decides which way a parabola opens.

questions.solution_text:
$y' = 8x - 9$
$y'' = 8$
The second derivative is the constant $8$, which is positive for every value of $x$.
So the curve is concave up for all $x$.

questions.question_text: For what values of $x$ is $y = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 11x - 4$ concave down?

options.why: Solved $12x - 6 > 0$, which is the condition for concave up.
Solved $12x < 6$ as $x < \tfrac{12}{6}$, dividing the wrong way round.
Both used the concave-up inequality and divided $12$ by $6$ instead of $6$ by $12$.

questions.question_text: For what values of $x$ is $y = x^{4} - 24x^{2} + 5$ concave up?

options.why: Solved $12x^{2} - 48 < 0$, which is the condition for concave down.
Took only the positive square root of $x^{2} > 4$ and left out the branch $x < -2$.
Solved $x^{2} > 12$, using the coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $y''$ instead of dividing the constant by it.

questions.question_text: For what values of $x$ is $y = xe^{2x}$ concave up?

options.why: Solved $4x + 4 < 0$, which is the condition for concave down.
Used $y' = e^{2x}(1 + 2x) > 0$, which gives where the curve is increasing, not where it is concave up.
Assumed that because $e^{2x} > 0$ the whole second derivative is positive, ignoring the factor $4x + 4$.
Read the part of the curve that bends like $\cap$ as the concave-up part.
Used the $x$-intercept of the curve instead of the point where the bending reverses.
Took the local maximum at $x = -2$ as the place where the concavity changes.

questions.solution_text:
Read the bending of the curve from left to right.
To the left the curve bends downwards like $\cap$, and to the right it bends upwards like $\cup$.
The bending reverses at $x = -1$.
The curve is concave up for $x > -1$.

questions.question_text: At the point where $x = 6$, a curve $y = f(x)$ has $f'(6) > 0$ and $f''(6) < 0$. Which statement describes the curve there?

options.text: Increasing, and increasing at a decreasing rate.
Increasing, and increasing at an increasing rate.
options.why: Read $f'' < 0$ as concave up, confusing the sign of the second derivative with the direction of the curve.
Used the sign of $f''$ to decide whether the curve rises or falls.

options.text: Decreasing, and decreasing at a decreasing rate.
options.why: Swapped the roles of $f'$ and $f''$ entirely.

questions.solution_text:
$f'(6) > 0$ means the gradient is positive, so the curve is increasing at $x = 6$.
$f''(6) < 0$ means the gradient is decreasing, so the curve is concave down at $x = 6$.
A positive gradient that is getting smaller means the curve rises less and less steeply.
So the curve is increasing at a decreasing rate.

questions.question_text: For what values of $k$ is $y = x^{3} + kx^{2} + 7x - 2$ concave down at the point where $x = 2$?

options.why: Solved $12 + 2k > 0$, which is the condition for concave up.
Solved $2k < -12$ as $k < -12$, forgetting to divide by $2$.
Both used the concave-up inequality and forgot to divide by $2$.
